title: Quitting the trumpet in 1934 because of gum disease
summary: He played until 1934, when gum disease and poor pay made him give up music altogether.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Oh yeah, after 1913. And I played with the food until 1934. Oh yeah. That's when you stopped? I stopped. I had a problem with my teeth. I had this pyrene disease. Oh yeah, gum. I was loose and I couldn't, didn't have no support for my lips. I had to leave the thing alone. Then I was kind of discouraged with it anyway, because that was making it harder to do by having these bad teeth. And he wasn't getting enough money. So I said, well, that's two things against me, not enough money and bad teeth. That's just where I leave it alone. You decided to stop playing music altogether? Altogether. You didn't play any other instruments? No, not since then. Never played enough. That's a long time ago. A long time ago. That's about almost forty years, ain't it? From 34 to now.
